<problem>
Fix an integer \(e\ge 0\). Throughout, \(\mathbb P(V)\) parametrizes one-dimensional complex subspaces of the fibres of a vector bundle \(V\), and \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(V)}(1)\) is the dual of the tautological line subbundle. Let
\[
X=\mathbb P_{\mathbb P^1}\bigl(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e)\bigr),\qquad \pi:X\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1.
\]
Let \(f\) be the divisor class of a fibre of \(\pi\), and let \(S\) be the section defined by the displayed summand \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e)\). Thus \(S^2=-e\), \(S\cdot f=1\), and \(f^2=0\). Set
\[
H=S+(3e+1)f,\qquad P=4H-f,
\]
\[
E_0=\mathcal O_X(5S-f)\oplus\mathcal O_X\bigl(-S+(12e+5)f\bigr),
\]
where \(\mathcal O_X(D)\) denotes the line bundle associated with a divisor \(D\). Write \(\bar\partial_0\) for the split Dolbeault operator of \(E_0\).

Suppose \((\bar\partial_j)_{j\ge1}\) is a sequence of smooth integrable Dolbeault operators on the underlying smooth complex bundle of \(E_0\). Thus \(\bar\partial_j^2=0\). Assume that \(\bar\partial_j-\bar\partial_0\), viewed as an endomorphism-valued \((0,1)\)-form, tends to zero in every finite \(C^m\) norm, measured using fixed smooth background metrics and connections. Let \(E_j\) denote the resulting holomorphic rank-two bundle.

Assume every \(E_j\) is ample and slope-stable with respect to \(P\). Here ampleness means that \(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(E_j^*)}(1)\) is ample; a line bundle is ample if some positive tensor power has a complete linear system giving a projective embedding. Slope-stability means that every nonzero coherent rank-one subsheaf \(\mathcal F\subset E_j\) satisfies
\[
c_1(\mathcal F)\cdot P<\frac{c_1(E_j)\cdot P}{2},
\]
where \(c_1\) is the first Chern class and the dot denotes intersection on \(X\).

Define the complex fourfolds
\[
U_j=\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X\oplus E_j)\setminus\mathbb P(\mathcal O_X),
\]
where the removed section comes from the first summand. For a complex fourfold \(U\), define \(\kappa(U)\) to be the least positive integer \(q\) for which there exist a smooth function \(\psi:U\to\mathbb R\) and a compact subset \(K\subset U\) such that every sublevel set \(\{\psi\le c\}\), for \(c\in\mathbb R\), is compact and the Levi form of \(\psi\) has at least \(5-q\) strictly positive eigenvalues at every point of \(U\setminus K\). The Levi form is the Hermitian form with matrix \((\partial^2\psi/\partial z_a\partial\bar z_b)\) in local holomorphic coordinates.

Determine \(\displaystyle\lim_{j\to\infty}\kappa(U_j)\).
</problem>

A complete answer to this problem: A complete answer must give the exact integer value of the limit, as a formula in e if necessary, and establish that the limit exists. It must apply to every sequence satisfying the hypotheses, resolving any possible dependence on the chosen sequence.

Their run ended: all agents idle, the judge found the proof complete. 99	## 3. A support-norm lemma

101	Here is the analytic device for the lower bound.

103	**Lemma.** Let \(E\) be a rank-two holomorphic bundle over a complex surface \(M\). Suppose \(\Omega\subset E\) is a neighbourhood of the zero section with compact closure, containing a uniform small disc bundle, and with smooth boundary. Suppose that, for a defining function
104	\[
105	\Omega=\{r<0\},
106	\]
107	the Levi form of \(r\) on the complex tangent space of \(\partial\Omega\) has at least two strictly negative eigenvalues.
108	
109	Then
110	\[
111	F(x,\xi)=
112	\max_{v\in\overline\Omega\cap E_x}|\xi(v)|,
113	\qquad \xi\in E_x^*,
114	\tag{8}
115	\]
116	is a continuous complex norm on each fibre, and \(\log F\) is plurisubharmonic on \(E^*\setminus0\).
117	
118	### Proof
119	
120	Positivity, complex homogeneity and the triangle inequality follow directly from (8), using the inner and outer disc bounds on \(\Omega\).
121	
122	We first verify a regularity point. Let \(v_0\) maximize (8) for \(\xi_0\ne0\). After changing its phase, assume
123	\[
124	\xi_0(v_0)=F(x_0,\xi_0)>0.
125	\]
126	Then \(v_0\in\partial\Omega\), and the outward half-space
127	\[
128	\operatorname{Re}\xi_0(v)>F(x_0,\xi_0)
129	\]
130	contains no point of \(\overline\Omega\cap E_{x_0}\).
131	
132	We claim
133	\[
134	d_vr(x_0,v_0)\ne0.
135	\tag{9}
136	\]
137	Otherwise, Taylor expansion on the outward half-space shows that the real vertical Hessian of \(r\) is nonnegative there. Since a quadratic form is even, it is nonnegative on all vertical vectors. Thus the vertical Levi form is semipositive on the complex two-dimensional vertical space.
138	
139	But that vertical space would lie in the complex tangent space of \(\partial\Omega\), which has dimension three. It must intersect every two-dimensional negative plane nontrivially, contradicting the two negative eigenvalues. This proves (9).
140	
141	Compactness gives upper semicontinuity of \(F\). At a maximizing point, (9) permits approximation by points in \(\Omega\cap E_{x_0}\), and those points remain in \(\Omega\) for nearby base points. This gives lower semicontinuity. Hence \(F\) is continuous.
142	
143	It remains to prove plurisubharmonicity. Work in holomorphic bundle coordinates and restrict \(\log F\) to an affine complex line
144	\[
145	t\longmapsto (x(t),\xi(t)).
146	\]
147	
148	If \(x(t)\) is constant, the submean inequality follows by choosing a maximizing \(v_0\) at the centre:
149	\[
150	\log F(0)=\log|\xi(0)v_0|
151	\le \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log|\xi(re^{i\theta})v_0|\,d\theta
152	\le \frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\log F(re^{i\theta})\,d\theta.
153	\]

155	Suppose now that \(x(t)\) is nonconstant. If the restriction were not subharmonic, there would be a smooth upper test \(\phi\), touching it at \(t=0\), with
156	\[
157	\phi_{t\bar t}(0)<0.
158	\]
159	Choose a maximizing \(v_0\) at \(t=0\), and set
160	\[
161	\rho(t,v)=\log|\xi(t)v|-\phi(t).
162	\]
163	Near \((0,v_0)\), this is smooth, since \(\xi(0)v_0\ne0\). The pulled-back domain satisfies
164	\[
165	\Omega\subset\{\rho\le0\},
166	\]
167	with equality at the contact point.

169	By (9), the pulled-back boundary is smooth. Boundary comparison gives
170	\[
171	d\rho=\lambda\,dr,\qquad
172	\mathcal L_\rho\le\lambda\mathcal L_r
173	\quad\text{on the common complex tangent},
174	\qquad \lambda>0.
175	\tag{10}
176	\]
177	The function \(\log|\xi(t)v|\) is pluriharmonic near the contact point, so

179	\mathcal L_\rho=-\phi_{t\bar t}(0)|dt|^2\ge0.
180	\]
181	Thus (10) forces \(\mathcal L_r\ge0\) on that complex tangent.

216	\]
217	Its ambient Levi form has at least three negative eigenvalues, hence its boundary complex-tangential Levi form has at least two.
218	
219	The lemma therefore supplies a continuous fibre norm \(F\) on \(E^*\) with \(\log F\) plurisubharmonic.

221	## 5. Such norms cannot occur along a sequence converging to \(A\oplus B\)
222	
223	Suppose, towards a contradiction, that infinitely many \(U_j\) admit three-positive-at-infinity exhaustions. Pass to that subsequence, and obtain norms \(F_j\) as above.
224	
225	Fix a smooth background norm on the underlying bundle \(E_0^*\). Rescale each \(F_j\) so that
226	\[
227	\max_{x,\ |\xi|=1}F_j(x,\xi)=1.
228	\tag{11}
229	\]
230	Thus
231	\[
232	F_j(x,\xi)\le|\xi|
233	\tag{12}
234	\]
235	everywhere.
236	
237	On sufficiently small coordinate charts choose holomorphic frames
238	\[
239	s_{j,\alpha,1},s_{j,\alpha,2}
240	\]

242	\[
243	s_{0,\alpha,1},s_{0,\alpha,2}
244	\]
245	adapted to \(A^*\oplus B^*\). Such frames follow from local solvability of the integrable matrix-valued \(\bar\partial\)-equation with parameters. 246	
247	Set
248	\[
249	u_{j,\alpha,i}=F_j(s_{j,\alpha,i})^2.
250	\]

252	\[
253	u_{j,\alpha,i}\longrightarrow u_{\alpha,i}
254	\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}.
255	\tag{13}
256	\]
257	
258	At least one limit is nonzero. Indeed, take points and unit vectors attaining (11). In a fixed local frame their coefficients are bounded. The submean inequality then gives a positive lower bound for its integral on a fixed relatively compact chart. This survives (13).

260	The limits glue diagonally. For example, if the limiting \(A^*\)-frames satisfy
261	\[
262	s_{0,\beta,1}=g_{\alpha\beta}s_{0,\alpha,1},
263	\]
264	then
265	\[
266	s_{j,\beta,1}-g_{\alpha\beta}s_{j,\alpha,1}\longrightarrow0
267	\]
268	smoothly. The triangle inequality and (12) yield
269	\[
270	F_j(s_{j,\beta,1})
271	-|g_{\alpha\beta}|F_j(s_{j,\alpha,1})
272	\longrightarrow0
273	\]
274	locally uniformly. Hence
275	\[
276	u_{\beta,1}=|g_{\alpha\beta}|^2u_{\alpha,1}.
277	\tag{14}
278	\]
279	The analogous statement holds for \(B^*\).
280	
281	Moreover, each nonzero limiting diagonal has plurisubharmonic logarithm. For every \(\delta>0\),
282	\[
283	\log(u_{j,\alpha,i}+\delta)
284	\]
285	is plurisubharmonic and converges in \(L^1_{\rm loc}\) to
286	\(\log(u_{\alpha,i}+\delta)\). Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) proves that
287	\(\log u_{\alpha,i}\) is plurisubharmonic, unless identically \(-\infty\).
288	
289	Thus a nonzero diagonal, together with (14), defines a singular negative metric on \(A^*\) or on \(B^*\). Its dual gives a positive curvature current representing \(c_1(A)\) or \(c_1(B)\). Both possibilities contradict (2).
290	
291	We have excluded every subsequence admitting a three-positive-at-infinity exhaustion. Therefore
292	\[
293	\kappa(U_j)\ge3
294	\]
295	for all sufficiently large \(j\). Combined with (7), this proves eventual equality and the asserted limit.
